title: writematrix
summary: Write numeric or string matrices to delimited text files.

gpu_support.notes: Runs on the host. Automatically resident values gather transparently; explicit gpuArray input requires RunMat mode.

description: `writematrix(A, filename)` serializes a numeric or string matrix to a delimited text file. Native integer matrices retain their exact decimal values.
behaviors: Accepts real numeric, logical, or string arrays with up to two dimensions (trailing singleton dimensions are ignored). Heterogeneous data requires `writecell` instead.
Default delimiters follow MATLAB: comma for `.csv`, tab for `.tsv`, whitespace for `.txt` and `.dat`, and comma for other extensions. Specify `'Delimiter', value` to override.
`'WriteMode'` supports `'overwrite'` (default) and `'append'`. Overwrite truncates existing files; append writes new rows to the end without inserting extra delimiters.
`'QuoteStrings'` accepts `'minimal'` (default), `'all'`, or `'none'`. Minimal quoting protects fields that contain the delimiter, a quote, or a line break.
RunMat mode also accepts logical and numeric zero/one aliases for `'QuoteStrings'`, the text-format options `'DecimalSeparator'` and `'LineEnding'`, and a bytes-written output.
`'FileType'` accepts `'delimitedtext'` or `'text'`. Spreadsheet output (`'spreadsheet'`) is not yet available and triggers a descriptive error consistent with MATLAB's messaging.
Spreadsheet output is not yet implemented. Sparse input is rejected.

examples.description: Save a numeric matrix to a CSV file
Export data with a custom semicolon delimiter
Append additional rows to an existing report

faqs.question: Which data types does `writematrix` support?
faqs.answer: Real numeric, logical, and string arrays up to two dimensions. For heterogenous content (mixed numbers and text) use `writecell` or `writetable`.

faqs.question: How are empty matrices handled?
faqs.answer: Zero-row or zero-column inputs produce either an empty file or blank line endings per MATLAB's behaviour. The file is still created or truncated according to `'WriteMode'`.

faqs.question: Can I write OTA spreadsheet formats like `.xlsx`?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Passing `'FileType','spreadsheet'` raises a descriptive error. Use MATLAB's table-based workflows or export delimited text instead.

faqs.question: How are embedded quotes in text fields escaped?
faqs.answer: With `'minimal'` or `'all'`, embedded double quotes are doubled. With `'none'`, text is written verbatim.

faqs.question: What happens if I choose `','` as both delimiter and decimal separator?
faqs.answer: RunMat mode honours the request without modification, even though the output may be ambiguous. Choose a different delimiter when using the `DecimalSeparator` extension.

faqs.question: Does `writematrix` change the working directory?
faqs.answer: No. Relative paths are resolved against the current RunMat working directory, and only the target file is touched.

faqs.question: How do I include header rows or variable names?
faqs.answer: `writematrix` focuses on numeric and string matrices. Use `writetable` for named variables.

gpu_residency: `writematrix` is a host file-I/O sink. Automatically resident values gather transparently before formatting; explicit `gpuArray` input requires RunMat mode.
gpu_behavior: The write executes on the host. Automatic residency is gathered through the owning provider, while explicit device intent is compatibility-gated before provider or file access.
